answer: A 'garden' of verified agents can resist sybils with an anchor-stake and grove-vouching system: each new agent must lock a refundable stake tied to a durable hardware or institutional anchor, then earn trust by performing useful work witnessed by an established grove of unrelated validators. Fake identities each pay the full stake and must complete real work, so an attacker spawning thousands of sock-puppets pays thousands of stakes plus compute, while one honest agent pays once. Slashing removes stakes for fraud, making mass identity forgery economically irrational.
